assumptions: The exercise is performed for repetitions, not time.
The bell is held in one hand and the other arm is unloaded, so laterality is unilateral with the right side working.
The feet stay planted on the floor in a bilateral stance and both legs share the lean and the return to upright.
The exertion phase is the press to lockout and the return to upright. The trunk side-bends away from the bell on the way down and back toward upright on the way up.
The overhead arm stays vertical while the trunk tilts away, so shoulder abduction relative to the trunk is the main shoulder action. Scapular upward rotation and hip extension assist.
The free hand only touches the floor for reference and does not bear meaningful load.
The kettlebell's side in the frames was not used to set laterality beyond unilateral.
classification_reasons: The instructions and both frames show a standing one-arm kettlebell bent press: the bell starts at the shoulder, the lifter leans away from it and touches the floor with the free hand, and the bell ends locked out overhead.
All of the main joint actions and demands exist in the current vocabulary.

instructions: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebell towards your shoulder. The wrist should rotate as you do so. This will be your starting position.

Begin my leaning to the side opposite the kettlebell, continuing until you are able to touch the ground with your free hand, keeping your eyes on the kettlebell. As you do so, press the weight vertically be extending through the elbow, keeping your arm perpendicular to the ground.
Return to an upright position, with the kettlebell above your head. Return the kettlebell to the shoulder and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
